desc:
You may write the string a one or more times in a row to form a longer string. Return the smallest number of copies of a such that b is a contiguous substring of the result. If no number of copies works, return -1.

For example, with a = "abc" and b = "cabcabca" the answer is 4, because "abcabcabcabc" contains b but three copies do not. With a = "abc" and b = "acb" the answer is -1.
constraints: Both strings consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Appending copies of a forever cannot help once the text is long enough. How many copies are certainly enough to be able to decide?
You need at least ceil(b.length / a.length) copies just for the length. Because b can start in the middle of a copy, one more copy may be needed, but no more than that.
Build the strings with k0 = ceil(|b| / |a|) and k0 + 1 copies and test each for b with a linear substring search (KMP); return the first that works, else -1.
editorial: Let k0 = ceil(|b| / |a|). With fewer than k0 copies the text is shorter than b, so no answer is below k0.

Suppose b occurs in some number of copies of a, starting inside copy number t (0-based) of the text. Then the same occurrence also exists if we delete the first t copies, because the text is periodic with period |a|. After that it begins inside the first copy and spans at most |b| characters, so it fits within ceil((|b| + |a| - 1) / |a|) copies, which is at most k0 + 1. Hence only k0 and k0 + 1 need testing.
Each test is a substring search. A KMP search (build the failure table of b, scan the repeated text) takes O(|a| · k0 + |b|) = O(|a| + |b|) time and avoids the quadratic worst case of naive matching.
